name: Fields
summary: Give goals a workspace’s own fields, such as a stage or a programme, to find and sort them by.

rebuild.builds: Fields, as a feature a workspace can switch off: a workspace defines up to six of its own fields on goals (a stage, a programme), each a list of values or free text; a goal has at most one value per field. No rule reads a field. Today it holds its tables (migration 0052) and its rule (tags-fields); its screens, its goal block, its filters, its sheet columns and its AI tools come next (TG1, TG2).
entry: The core saves a module's records through module_tables and src/core/records.ts (stage 2), so the module's two tables need nothing from any core rule.
exit: fieldProblem and valueProblem give the tags-fields rule's worked examples (src/modules/tags/rules.test.ts).
The database refuses a field name over 40 characters, a kind other than list or text, a list of no values or over 20, and a value over 80 characters (migration 0052's checks, src/spec/limits.ts).
gaps: Its two tables, faro.goal_fields and faro.goal_field_values (migration 0052, on module_tables as module tags), are made one merge ahead of the code that uses them; records.ts claims them in TG1, and module.json lists them then.

Nothing draws a field yet: Workspace → Fields, the goal's Fields block, the MCP tools list_fields and set_goal_fields, and the switch's off states are TG1; the filters, saved views, Data's column and the sheet's columns with the import's question are TG2 (docs/design/round-4/tags/spec.md, section 10). Until then switching Fields off changes nothing anyone can see.
